name: MS-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Trent Kelly running with a large cash advantage
No polls or expert ratings; markets price Kelly at ~96%
model.rationale: Kelly holds a deeply Republican seat, out-raised Johnson roughly two-to-one, and prediction markets give him about a 96% chance of winning. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays safely Republican.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Johnson within single digits, or major outside spending against Kelly, would warrant moving this toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Trent Kelly seeks another term in a northeastern Mississippi district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan baseline near R+18. Kelly was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with a clear financial edge, having raised about $1 million and holding roughly $864,000 on hand. Democrat Cliff Johnson has run a credible fundraising effort for a challenger in this territory, bringing in about $551,000, but starts with far less cash and no outside spending on either side has been reported.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing, which gives Kelly roughly a 96% chance of reelection. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot. The district's partisan makeup and the incumbent's resources make an upset unlikely.
